description: 3D-PV-Locator is the research authors' Docker-based Python workflow for detecting rooftop photovoltaic systems and estimating their three-dimensional properties. It combines aerial images and CityGML buildings to produce GeoJSON footprints with estimated area, capacity, tilt and azimuth. The documented application uses German North Rhine-Westphalia imagery at ten-centimetre resolution; dates and coverage follow the selected imagery and building source. Code is free under MIT and is configured through YAML. A limitation is that the linked training data and weights use an AWS requester-pays bucket, so code access does not make every runtime input cost-free. Roof matching and geocoding also require suitable local inputs. The tool supports preparation of distributed-generation inventories for electricity simulations. OpenDSS (platform-opendss) provides related distribution-network analysis. The Applied Energy article describes the method; no imagery, weights or model archive was downloaded.
name: 3D-PV-Locator rooftop photovoltaic detection
